sources.title: Console Commands (Killing Floor) - Tripwire Interactive Wiki
Hosting A Killing Floor (2009) Dedicated Server in 2023
2 KF1 players ruining my friend's experience :: Killing Floor General Discussions

notes: Killing Floor (2009) runs on Unreal Engine 2.5 and has no RCON and no admin HTTP/JSON API, so there is no text-command pipe to send anything down - hence transport 'none' and no commands. Tripwire's own wiki documents exactly two admin surfaces: WebAdmin, an HTML panel on TCP 8075 (Applications[0]=xWebAdmin at path /ServerAdmin, turned on with bEnabled=True under [UWeb.WebServer] in System/KillingFloor.ini, admin credentials from [Engine.AccessControl] AdminPassword or xAdmin.ini), and the in-game client console, where an admin types 'AdminLogin <password>' and then 'Admin <command>'. Kick, KickBan and PlayerList do exist as server-side admin commands, but they are only reachable through that authenticated game client or the WebAdmin's buttons: WebAdmin is a form/session HTML UI with no documented endpoints and no basic/bearer auth, and PlayerList only writes to the server log rather than returning a response, so neither can be driven as a command transport. The dedicated server process (KFServer.exe on Windows, ucc-bin on Linux) prints a log but no source found documents a stdin command prompt. Bans persist in System/KillingFloor.ini under [Engine.AccessControl] as BannedIDs= entries with bBanByID=True, and a restart is needed for a hand edit to take effect. Confidence is low on that file format specifically: the UE2 Engine.AccessControl source and the BeyondUnreal wiki agree that BannedIDs is a globalconfig array<string> and that bBanByID switches ID bans on, but only a single community post documents the Killing-Floor-specific line spelling 'BannedIDs=<SteamID64> <PlayerName>'. The transport finding itself is supported by several independent sources. The dedicated server app id is split by platform - 215360 (Linux, recorded here) and 215350 (Win32) - and this is Killing Floor 1, not Killing Floor 2 (app 232090), which has a different WebAdmin.
